content.text:
In the care_fe repo at /Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe, explore the Playwright tests under `tests/` (especially tests/billing/ and tests/facility/) that cover the pharmacy "bill medications by prescriptions" flow. I need to add a test for a new `NoActiveAccountWarningDialog` that appears on the Bill Medications page (route for BillMedicationsByPrescriptions) when the patient has NO active+open billing account.

Report back, thoroughly:
1. The full list of test files under tests/billing/ and any pharmacy-related test files, with their paths.
2. The complete contents (or detailed summary with code) of the test file(s) that navigate to the bill medications / pharmacy dispense flow — how they navigate there (URL patterns), what fixtures/helpers they use.
3. Contents of tests/helper/ and tests/support/ relevant helpers (getFacilityId, getPatientId, getEncounterId, any pharmacy helpers, any account creation helpers).
4. How tests create or check billing accounts (search for "account" in tests/).
5. The route definition in src/Routers for the BillMedicationsByPrescriptions page (exact URL path with params).
6. The i18n strings `no_active_account_found`, `no_active_account_warning_description`, `go_to_accounts`, `proceed` from public/locale/en.json.
7. Key patterns from tests/PLAYWRIGHT_GUIDE.md relevant to asserting on dialogs/alert-dialogs.

Do not write any code, just report findings.
I’ll locate the pharmacy and billing tests, then trace their navigation, fixtures, account setup, and dialog assertions. I’ll report findings only, without changing files.

The billing directory has two specs; pharmacy coverage may live in tests with other filenames. I’ll search test contents for dispense navigation and account handling next. Terminal tools aren’t available here, so I can’t query Entire or Graphify history.

The search hasn’t found a test that navigates to Bill Medications or patient dispensing. It did find pharmacy inventory tests and an account-transfer spec with API helpers that could support the new test. I’ll check the routes and setup dependencies to confirm that gap.

The warning specifically checks for an account with both `status=active` and `billing_status=open`. The shared account setup only filters by active status, so it can’t guarantee the new test’s precondition. I’ll read the ID helpers and nested route definition next, and distinguish the actual guide guidance from dialog patterns in existing specs.

The prescription-billing route is defined inside `LocationLayout`, beneath the facility/location router. “Proceed” dismisses the warning; “Go to Accounts” navigates to the facility account list with `patient_filter`. I’ll finish by checking pharmacy navigation examples, prescription setup, and existing alert-dialog assertions.

There’s no dedicated patient-dispense or prescription-billing test in the current suite. The closest templates are inventory specs for finding the pharmacy location, prescription specs for creating medication requests, and billing specs for account state. I’ll collect the remaining file list and setup details, then summarize them in the seven sections you requested.

The setup project normally gives the shared patient a billing account, and tests run in parallel, so changing that patient’s accounts could affect other specs. The account-transfer test avoids this by creating a dedicated patient. I’ll verify the remaining location and account templates before closing the report.

The useful pieces are now clear: ID helpers load setup metadata, API helpers use the saved admin token, and account creation/update helpers are local to the account-transfer spec. I’ll check prescription editing and data exports once more so the report includes all adjacent medication test files.

**Main Finding**
There is **no existing test that reaches “Bill Medications by Prescriptions” or patient medication dispensing**. Existing coverage reaches the Prescription Queue, pharmacy inventory transfers, and encounter prescriptions. No files were changed or tests run; findings below come from current source.

**1. Test Inventory**
All files directly under `tests/billing/`:
- [tests/billing/paymentSheetUrl.spec.ts](tests/billing/paymentSheetUrl.spec.ts): payment/credit-note sheet URL persistence and dismissal.
- [tests/billing/updateAccountPermission.spec.ts](tests/billing/updateAccountPermission.spec.ts): account editing/rebalancing permissions for facility admin, admin, and nurse.

Additional facility billing specs:
- [tests/facility/billing/accountTransfer.spec.ts](tests/facility/billing/accountTransfer.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/billing/paymentReconciliation.spec.ts](tests/facility/billing/paymentReconciliation.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/billing/invoiceList.spec.ts](tests/facility/billing/invoiceList.spec.ts)

Pharmacy navigation/inventory and medication-related specs:
- [tests/facility/services/locations/locations.spec.ts](tests/facility/services/locations/locations.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toDispatch.spec.ts](tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toDispatch.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toReceive.spec.ts](tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toReceive.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/services/service.spec.ts](tests/facility/services/service.spec.ts): creates a pharmacy-type service, tests service switching.
- [tests/facility/patient/encounter/medicine/prescriptionCreate.spec.ts](tests/facility/patient/encounter/medicine/prescriptionCreate.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/patient/encounter/medicine/prescriptionEdit.spec.ts](tests/facility/patient/encounter/medicine/prescriptionEdit.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/patient/encounter/structuredQuestions/medicationRequest.spec.ts](tests/facility/patient/encounter/structuredQuestions/medicationRequest.spec.ts)
- [tests/facility/settings/activityDefinition/activityDefinitionEdit.spec.ts](tests/facility/settings/activityDefinition/activityDefinitionEdit.spec.ts): incidental “main pharmacy” service selection, not dispensing.

**2. Closest Flow Templates**
All pharmacy/medication specs above use `tests/.auth/user.json`.
- **toDispatch:** `getFacilityId()` → `/facility/${facilityId}/services/` → “Main Pharmacy” link → “Pharmacy” link. Extracts location ID with `/facility/${facilityId}/locations/([^/]+)/medication_requests`. Builds `/facility/${facilityId}/locations/${pharmacyLocationId}`, then visits `/inventory/internal/dispatch`. Local `setupInitialData()` and `createStockRequest()` create a lab stock request containing Paracetamol, approve it, create pharmacy delivery orders, select stock, and verify receiving/completion. **This is stock dispatch, not patient dispensing.**
- **toReceive:** follows the same service links, then extracts the lab location from `/locations/([^/]+)/service_requests`; tests `/inventory/internal/receive`, creating and completing stock requests from Pharmacy.
- **locations:** creates a pharmacy service through `createHealthcareService()`, opens its Pharmacy location, asserts “Prescription Queue”, and tests location switching. It never selects a prescription or bills medications.
- **prescriptionCreate / prescriptionEdit:** visit `/facility/${facilityId}/encounters/patients/all?created_date_after=…&created_date_before=…&status=in_progress`, select the first “View Encounter”, then “Medicines”. Create uses the “Create” link, medication picker, dose/frequency/instructions/notes, and Submit; verifies the success toast and prescription table. Edit additionally locates a dated prescription card, edits/removes medication, and verifies inactive medications. Both use faker and [prescriptionTestData.ts](tests/facility/patient/encounter/medicine/prescriptionTestData.ts), exporting `medicineNames`, `frequencies`, and `instructions`; neither captures prescription IDs for billing.
- **medicationRequest:** uses all three ID helpers and directly visits `/facility/${facilityId}/patient/${patientId}/encounter/${encounterId}/questionnaire/medication_request`; fills medication fields, submits, then verifies the named “Medication History” dialog. Its local `selectDuration()` selects an exact-match duration suggestion.

**3. Relevant Helpers**
- [tests/support/facilityId.ts](tests/support/facilityId.ts), [patientId.ts](tests/support/patientId.ts), [encounterId.ts](tests/support/encounterId.ts), and [accountId.ts](tests/support/accountId.ts) export their respective `get…Id(): string` functions. Each reads `{id}` from `tests/.auth/{entity}Meta.json`, caches it in module memory, and synchronously runs its setup spec through `execSync()` if the file is missing. Invalid JSON/missing IDs throw; they do **not** regenerate invalid existing metadata. Encounter setup also runs the patient setup spec.
- [tests/setup/patient.setup.ts](tests/setup/patient.setup.ts) selects an existing planned/in-progress encounter from the last 90 days and saves patient/encounter IDs extracted from its URL; it does not create a fresh patient.
- [tests/helper/utils.ts](tests/helper/utils.ts): `getApiUrl()` returns `REACT_CARE_API_URL || "http://localhost:9000"`; `getApiHeaders()` reads `care_access_token` from the first origin in saved **admin** storage and returns Bearer authorization plus JSON content type. `expectedSlug()` lowercases, hyphenates whitespace, and truncates to 25 characters.
- [tests/helper/ui.ts](tests/helper/ui.ts): reusable command/value-set/location selectors scope to dialogs or popovers and wait for visibility; `expectToast()` asserts text within `.toaster.group`; `clickTabOrMenuItem()` supports responsive navigation.
- [tests/helper/questionnaire.ts](tests/helper/questionnaire.ts): `submitForm()`, `submitAndExpectSuccess()`, field/visibility helpers, and submitted-value assertions. No dedicated pharmacy or billing-account helper exists under `tests/helper/`.
- [tests/facility/services/helpers.ts](tests/facility/services/helpers.ts): `createHealthcareService(page, facilityId, serviceName, servicesUrl)` creates a Pharmacy-type service attached to a Pharmacy location; `toggleSidebar(page, expand)` controls navigation layout. No shared location-ID or prescription-ID helper exists.

**4. Billing Account Setup**
[tests/setup/patientAccount.setup.ts](tests/setup/patientAccount.setup.ts) visits `facility/${facilityId}/patient/${patientId}/accounts?status=active`, checks “Go to account”, and either opens an existing account or creates one using `faker.finance.accountName()`, “Name *”, and “Create”. It extracts `/account/([a-f0-9-]+)` and saves account metadata. **It filters active status only, not open billing status.**
[accountTransfer.spec.ts](tests/facility/billing/accountTransfer.spec.ts#L17) has local, non-exported API helpers: `createAccount()` POSTs `/api/v1/facility/${facilityId}/account/` with `{name,status,billing_status,patient,service_period:{start:ISODate}}`; `updateAccount()` PUTs the detail endpoint with account data plus updates; `getAccount()` GETs the detail endpoint. `createPatient()` fetches a government organization and POSTs a unique patient. Setup creates active accounts with `open`, `billing`, and `carecomplete_notbilled`, plus nine combinations of non-active statuses and those billing statuses; teardown deactivates the three active accounts.
Other account matches are permission/payment specs, [backButton.spec.ts](tests/facility/components/backButton.spec.ts), and unrelated user “Delete Account”/login wording. None checks the pharmacy’s active+open account condition. **Avoid mutating the shared patient’s accounts:** [playwright.config.ts](playwright.config.ts) enables parallel tests and locally depends on setup, including patient-account setup.

**5. Exact Route And Warning Behavior**
[FacilityRoutes.tsx](src/Routers/routes/FacilityRoutes.tsx#L49) delegates `/facility/:facilityId/locations/:locationId*` to [LocationLayout.tsx](src/pages/Facility/locations/LocationLayout.tsx#L64), which defines:
```text
/facility/:facilityId/locations/:locationId/medication_requests/patient/:patientId/bill/prescriptions/:prescriptionIds
```
`prescriptionIds` is comma-separated and split into an array; this route has no encounter parameter. [BillMedicationsByPrescriptions.tsx](src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/BillMedicationsByPrescriptions.tsx) renders the warning alongside its billing shell. [NoActiveAccountWarningDialog.tsx](src/pages/Facility/billing/account/components/NoActiveAccountWarningDialog.tsx#L37) GETs accounts with `{patient:patientId,limit:1,status:"active",billing_status:"open"}` and opens after fetching completes when `count === 0`. “Proceed” only dismisses it, without immediately creating an account; “Go to Accounts” navigates to `/facility/${facilityId}/billing/account?patient_filter=${patientId}`.

**6. Exact English Strings**
From [public/locale/en.json](public/locale/en.json#L3683): `no_active_account_found` = **“No active account found”**; `no_active_account_warning_description` = **“This patient does not have an active billing account. Proceeding with this action will create a new billing account for the patient.”**; `go_to_accounts` = **“Go to Accounts”**; `proceed` = **“Proceed”**.

**7. Dialog Assertion Patterns**
[tests/PLAYWRIGHT_GUIDE.md](tests/PLAYWRIGHT_GUIDE.md#L319) recommends visibility/hidden assertions, role/name button selection, navigation waits, authenticated storage, and unique test data. It has **no dedicated alert-dialog section**. The concrete alert-dialog template is [activityDefinitionDelete.spec.ts](tests/facility/settings/activityDefinition/activityDefinitionDelete.spec.ts#L46): select `page.getByRole("alertdialog")`, assert visibility and description, then click a button scoped inside it. [paymentSheetUrl.spec.ts](tests/billing/paymentSheetUrl.spec.ts#L24) instead filters ordinary dialogs by heading and asserts disappearance/URL changes. For this warning, the corresponding assertion shape is:
```typescript
const dialog = page.getByRole("alertdialog", { name: "No active account found" });
await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
await expect(dialog.getByText("This patient does not have an active billing account. Proceeding with this action will create a new billing account for the patient.")).toBeVisible();
await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Proceed", exact: true }).click();
await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
```
Use separate coverage for “Go to Accounts” and its filtered URL, plus an active+open account negative case. For that negative case, wait for the account query to finish before asserting absence, since the component initially renders nothing while fetching.

In /Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe, investigate the pharmacy prescription queue → bill medications UI flow and the APIs behind it.

Report:
1. `src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/PrescriptionQueue.tsx` — what it lists (API endpoint + query params), how a user selects a patient/prescriptions, and what button/link navigates to the `/medication_requests/patient/:patientId/bill/prescriptions/:prescriptionIds` route. Include exact visible button/link text (i18n keys and their English values from public/locale/en.json).
2. `src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/PrescriptionsPreviewPage.tsx` — same: what's on it, what button navigates to the bill route.
3. `src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/BillMedicationsShell.tsx` — what it renders (headings, buttons) so I can assert the page loaded. Give exact i18n keys + English values for headings.
4. `src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/modes/usePrescriptionsMode.*` — what queries it runs.
5. The medication request API: `src/types/emr/medicationRequest/medicationRequestApi.ts` (or similar) — the create/list endpoints and paths. Also how the pharmacy prescription queue filters medication requests (what status/fields make a prescription appear in the queue).
6. How to find the pharmacy location id for the fixture facility via API — look at `src/types/location/locationApi.ts` and how PrescriptionQueue/locations pages list locations (e.g. form=... or mode= query params). Report the exact endpoint + params used by tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toDispatch.spec.ts to resolve a pharmacy location id, including the UI steps it uses.
7. Whether `tests/setup/` has any spec that creates a pharmacy service/location fixture, and what `tests/.auth/*Meta.json` files exist / are produced.

Read-only; do not modify files. Give concrete code snippets for the key parts.
I’ll trace the queue, preview, and billing pages, then check their API definitions and fixture setup. I’ll keep this read-only and extract the English labels needed for assertions.

The queue lists prescription summaries, not individual medication requests. Patient filtering enables prescription selection; the preview page then offers billing for active prescriptions. I’ll check the link labels and billing-page queries next.

The queue has two billing links: “Bill Now” on an unfiltered active row and “Bill Selected Prescriptions” after patient filtering. The dispatch test resolves the location ID from UI navigation, not a direct API call; I’ll trace the API requests behind those service/location links.

Billing fetches each selected prescription by ID, then filters its medications locally. The setup specs mention facility, patient, encounter, and account metadata, but no pharmacy fixture creation. I’ll verify the fixture source and the location-list filters before wrapping up.

The locale value for `bill_selected_prescriptions` is “Bill Selected Rx,” and the active tab is labeled “Billing Pending.” Billing waits for the prescription fetches to finish before showing “Bill Medications,” so that heading is a useful loaded-page assertion.

The service page provides location IDs in its `locations` array, which is the API path behind the dispatch test’s “Main Pharmacy” → “Pharmacy” clicks. The queue itself sends no location filter, so its results are facility-wide even though it is opened under a location route.

An active prescription’s status determines whether it appears on “Billing Pending”; medication statuses are filtered later during billing. That filter keeps `active`, `on_hold`, `draft`, and `unknown` medications, and deselects those already fully dispensed. I’ll finish by checking the creation payload and setup dependencies.

The medication upsert handler creates an active parent prescription for new medication requests and groups them with a shared `alternate_identifier`. There is no pharmacy service/location setup spec; the tests rely on existing fixtures. I’m checking the last query details and metadata file shapes now.

There is no `form=pharmacy` filter in the location type definitions. To match the test, resolve “Main Pharmacy” through the healthcare-service API and select “Pharmacy” from its locations; the generic location picker uses `mode=kind` and name filtering. I’ll include both paths and distinguish the test’s actual requests.

I have the requested flow and fixture details. The final report will separate queue visibility from medication billing eligibility, show the exact English labels, and include the test’s navigation and API equivalents. This is based on source inspection; I haven’t run the UI or backend.

The preview table also has a per-prescription billing action in its overflow menu, alongside the page-level “Start Billing” link. I’ll include its exact label so the report covers both ways to reach billing.

Read-only source inspection; no files changed or runtime/API calls made. English labels below come from [public/locale/en.json](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/public/locale/en.json#L1020).

**1. Prescription Queue**
[PrescriptionQueue.tsx](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/PrescriptionQueue.tsx#L164) lists **prescription summaries**, one row per prescription: patient, prescriber/date, encounter class/status/current location, tags, and actions. Its API is `GET /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/medication_prescription/summary/`, defined in [prescriptionApi.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/types/emr/prescription/prescriptionApi.ts#L46).
```ts
queryFn: query.debounced(prescriptionApi.summary, {
  pathParams: { facilityId },
  queryParams: {
    status: currentTab, patient_external_id: qParams.patient_external_id,
    encounter_class: qParams.encounter_class,
    tags: qParams.tags, tags_behavior: qParams.tags_behavior,
    created_date_after: qParams.created_date_after
      ? dateTimeQueryString(new Date(qParams.created_date_after)) : undefined,
    created_date_before: qParams.created_date_before
      ? dateTimeQueryString(new Date(qParams.created_date_before), true) : undefined,
    limit: resultsPerPage, offset: ((qParams.page || 1) - 1) * resultsPerPage,
  },
}),
```
Default: `status=active&limit=14&offset=0`. Undefined filters are omitted. **No location filter is sent.** Tabs: `prescription_status__active` → “Billing Pending”; `prescription_status__completed` → “Completed”; `prescription_status__cancelled` → “Cancelled”. Heading: `prescription_queue` → “Prescription Queue”.
Select a patient through `PatientIdentifierFilter` or click a patient-name cell. Both set `patient_external_id` and `patient_name`. With a patient selected and the active tab open, all returned prescriptions **on the current page** are auto-selected; individual checkboxes/name cells toggle selection, and `select_all` → “Select All” toggles the page.
[Billing links](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/PrescriptionQueue.tsx#L348): `bill_selected_prescriptions` → **“Bill Selected Rx”** uses selected comma-separated IDs; an unfiltered active row has `bill_now` → **“Bill Now”** using that row’s ID. Zero selection visually disables the selected links. Preview links: `preview_selected_rx` → “Preview Selected Rx” and `view_rx` → “View Rx”.
```tsx
<Link href={`/medication_requests/patient/${qParams.patient_external_id}/bill/prescriptions/${selectedPrescriptionIds.join(",")}`}>
  {t("bill_selected_prescriptions")}<ArrowRightIcon />
</Link>
```
These links resolve under `/facility/{facilityId}/locations/{locationId}`; [LocationLayout.tsx](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/locations/LocationLayout.tsx#L66) splits `prescriptionIds` by commas.

**2. Prescription Preview**
[PrescriptionsPreviewPage.tsx](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/PrescriptionsPreviewPage.tsx#L45) fetches each prescription, then displays `prescription_preview` → **“Prescription Preview”**, patient header, medication search, dispense-status filter, prescription medication tables, and total/complete/partial/incomplete prescription counts. Search/status filtering is local.
Its billing link appears only when at least one loaded prescription has `status=active`:
```tsx
<Link href={`/medication_requests/patient/${patientId}/bill/prescriptions/${activePrescriptionIds.join(",")}`}>
  {t("start_billing")}<ShortcutBadge actionId="billing-action" /><ArrowRightIcon className="size-4" />
</Link>
```
`start_billing` → **“Start Billing”**. An additional-prescriptions card offers `show_all` → “Show all”, which navigates to **preview**, not billing. Each active prescription’s [table overflow menu](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/components/PrescriptionsPreviewTable.tsx#L219) also has `bill_prescription` → **“Bill Prescription”**, navigating to the full billing URL for that single prescription.

**3. Billing Shell**
[BillMedicationsShell.tsx](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/BillMedicationsShell.tsx#L27) returns `<Loading />` while `!mode.encounter || mode.isLoading`. Once ready, its visible **h4 heading** is `bill_medications` → **“Bill Medications”**, followed by patient header, optional unbilled-prescriptions card, and the billing form.
[Form](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/BillMedicationsForm.tsx#L81) contains prescription groups, medicine/lot/quantity/price controls, optional `other_items` → “Other Items”, and an `add_medication` → “Add Medication” picker. Column labels: `medicine` → “Medicine”; `select_lot` → “Select Lot”; `expiry` → “Expiry”; `quantity` → “Quantity”; `price` → “Price”; `all_given_question` → “All Given?”; `actions` → “Actions”. These are grid labels, not heading elements.
[Footer](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/BillMedicationsFooter.tsx#L76): `estimated_total` → “Estimated Total”; `cancel` → “Cancel”; `bill_selected` → **“Bill Selected”**, becoming `billing` → “Billing” during submission. The optional card uses `include_all` → “Include all”.
```ts
await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Bill Medications", exact: true })).toBeVisible();
await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Bill Selected", exact: true })).toBeVisible();
```

**4. Prescription-Mode Queries**
[usePrescriptionsMode.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/modes/usePrescriptionsMode.ts#L27) directly runs one query per supplied ID:
```ts
queries: prescriptionIds.map((prescriptionId) => ({
  queryKey: ["prescription", patientId, prescriptionId],
  queryFn: query(prescriptionApi.get, { pathParams: { patientId, id: prescriptionId } }),
})),
```
Endpoint: `GET /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/prescription/{id}/`, **no query params**. The first available prescription supplies the encounter; any query’s `isFetching` keeps the mode loading.
Indirectly, [useBillMedications](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/utils/useBillMedications.ts#L42) calls [useDefaultBillingAccount](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/types/billing/account/hooks/useDefaultBillingAccount.ts#L20): `GET /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/account/?ordering=-created_date&patient={patientId}&limit=1&offset=0&status=active&billing_status=open`.
The rendered [UnbilledPrescriptionsCard](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/billMedications/UnbilledPrescriptionsCard.tsx#L33) additionally requests `GET /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/prescription/?status=active&facility={facilityId}&limit=100`, excluding included IDs locally. It does **not** send `encounterId` as a filter.

**5. Medication API**
[medicationRequestApi.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/types/emr/medicationRequest/medicationRequestApi.ts#L5): list is `GET /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/request/`, default `ordering=-created_date`; declared filters are `encounter`, `prescription`, `product_type`, and `medications_only`. Creation/upsert is **POST `/api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/request/upsert/`**, not POST to the list endpoint. Update is `PUT /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/request/{id}/`.
The [questionnaire handler](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/components/Questionnaire/structured/handlers.ts#L65) sends `{ datapoints: [...] }`; new requests include:
```ts
create_prescription: {
  ...medication.create_prescription,
  status: PrescriptionStatus.active,
  alternate_identifier: prescriptionIdentifier,
},
```
It also sets `encounter`, `patient`, and requester ID; the shared identifier groups the new medications. Normal [medication defaults](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/types/emr/medicationRequest/medicationRequest.ts#L995) include `status="active"` and `intent="order"`.
**Queue visibility filters parent prescription status**, not individual medication status/intent/dispense status. Billing locally retains medication statuses `active`, `on_hold`, `draft`, `unknown`, skips empty groups, and initially selects medications with `dispense_status !== "complete"`. Backend summary inclusion rules beyond the supplied filters cannot be confirmed from this frontend repository.

**6. Pharmacy Location**
[locationApi.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/types/location/locationApi.ts#L12) lists `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/location/`, default `ordering=sort_index`. The [location switcher](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/components/ui/sidebar/facility/location/location-switcher.tsx#L164) uses `mode=kind`, `limit`, `offset`, optional `name`, optional `parent`, and conditional `mine=true`. An API equivalent for searching is `?ordering=sort_index&mode=kind&name=Pharmacy&limit=100&offset=0`; verify the returned name. **There is no pharmacy form option.**
[toDispatch.spec.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/tests/facility/services/locations/inventory/toDispatch.spec.ts#L51) does not directly call this API:
```ts
await page.goto(`/facility/${facilityId}/services/`);
await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Main Pharmacy" }).click();
await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Pharmacy" }).click();
pharmacyLocationId = page.url().match(
  new RegExp(`/facility/${facilityId}/locations/([^/]+)/medication_requests`),

```
Its backing requests are [service list](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/FacilityServices.tsx#L27): `GET /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/healthcare_service/?limit=12&offset=0` on the default first page; then [service detail](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/src/pages/Facility/services/HealthcareServiceShow.tsx#L119): `GET /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/healthcare_service/{serviceId}/`, **no params**. Resolve “Main Pharmacy”, then read its `locations` entry named “Pharmacy” and take its `id`. The location link also shows `view_prescriptions` → “View Prescriptions”.

**7. Setup Fixtures**
**No pharmacy service/location creation spec exists in setup.** [facility.setup.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/tests/setup/facility.setup.ts#L6) selects existing “Facility with Patient”; [patient.setup.ts](/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/tests/setup/patient.setup.ts#L8) selects an existing writable encounter.
